Monica,

We're seeing a severe production regression on lineage.workflows across our EU region beginning 09:10 UTC — p99 latency jumped from ~120ms to >4s and we've observed a 12% 5xx rate for model-inference requests. This started right after your recent config push to our reserved pool (we got a notice about a KV cache policy update).

Immediate impact: several customer jobs timed out (retries amplified), and the UI reports timeouts for dataset preview. We need an urgent rollback or mitigation. Attached is a sample trace and screenshots from our SRE console.

Can you please escalate to engineering and let us know ETA for a hotfix? We are in an all-hands on-call.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: sudden latency spikes / 5xx — production impact

Quick summary from infra: in the affected pool we see a ~40% increase in KV cache evictions starting 09:08 UTC. Evictions are correlated with long-running HOL (head-of-line) blocking in the short-batching lane — lanes are starving and long requests are holding KV locks for extended sequences, which causes downstream batches to stall and backpressure into the HTTP workers (5xx from timeouts).

Immediate mitigations we can apply (low risk -> higher):
1) Reduce per-client max concurrency on that pool (throttle long sequences) — low-risk, quick.
2) Bump KV cache capacity for MeridianAI to add headroom and reduce eviction churn.
3) Temporarily disable the aggressive LRU-prefetch eviction policy we rolled out last night; revert to stable policy.
4) Pin their traffic to a model variant with smaller kv slice size (reduces lock hold times) — needs coordination.

I'm pushing logs and a snapshot: kv_eviction_snapshot.txt attached.

Rishi
Infra Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-08-09T11:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: sudden latency spikes / 5xx — production impact

Adding ops notes. We've seen similar surface area when prefetching + LRU eviction interact under mixed request lengths — the prefetch pushes entries into kv sets that then get evicted aggressively, causing repeated misses and amplified KV lock contention. In this case the recent policy change prioritized batch throughput but reduced isolation for tenant hot-keys.

Proposed hot plan (execute in order):
- T+0: Rollback eviction policy for MeridianAI and pause prefetching for their tenant (30s).
- T+5m: Increase cache allocation by 20% for the pool and transiently relax eviction frequency.
- T+15m: Apply a prefix-based lease for their top-50 hot keys (protect against eviction churn).
- T+30m: Monitor p50/p95/p99 and error rate. If stable, plan a controlled rollback to the new policy in staging with synthetic workload.

Risk note: prefix lease is intrusive but limited in scope — requires a quick DB-migration-style toggle.

Evelyn
Platform Ops — Redwood Inference

- Paused tenant prefetching
- Provisioned +20% KV cache capacity on their pool (temporary)

Caroline: can you validate whether 5xx rate is dropping on your side? We'll continue monitoring and will keep this channel updated.

Monica

- Mitigation executed; p99 down to ~220ms and 5xx reduced to 0.9% as of 16:30 PDT.
- Root cause preliminary: mis-scoped rollout of the LRU-prefetch eviction policy combined with tenant hot-key patterns — led to persistent eviction churn and long KV lock holds for mixed-length sequences.
- Next 48h actions (owners):
  * Rishi/Evelyn: implement tenant-isolation guardrails and canary with synthetic hot-key workload (owner: Rishi)
  * Jonas: add per-tenant prefetch toggle and improve alerting for eviction churn (owner: Jonas)
  * Monica: coordinate a post-mortem and customer comms with Meridian (owner: Monica)
  * Finance: standby for potential credit — waiting on final impact window (owner: Marissa)

Caroline: we'll circulate a short post-incident report and schedule a 1:1 review tomorrow. Thanks for working with us through the incident.

Marissa Cole
